dedupe_keys.name: spatial and temporal analysis of extreme sea level and storm surge events around the coastline of the uk

description: Spatial and temporal analysis of extreme sea level and storm surge events around the coastline of the UK is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ivan D. Haigh et al. In this paper we analyse the spatial footprint and temporal clustering of extreme sea level and skew surge events around the UK coast over the last 100 years (1915–2014). The vast majority of the extreme sea level events are generated by moderate, not extreme skew surges, combined with spring astronomical high tides. Coverage: national (GB); published in 2016. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The paper's page was read, but no repository address could be taken from its machine-readable metadata, so the record links to the article, whose Data Records section names where the data sit. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
